scenes.title: The shift
scenes.goal: The viewer expects a mental-model change, not a syntax tour.
scenes.visual: Split screen: a React component re-renders top to bottom on the left; a Vue component stays still on the right while one dependency line lights up. Headline: 'how state changes propagate'.

lines.text: You already know React.
The biggest shift in Vue is how state changes propagate.

scenes.title: Snapshot versus tracking
scenes.goal: React re-runs with a snapshot; Vue tracks reads and updates dependents.
scenes.visual: Left panel 'React': a stack of render snapshots, each a full function call. Right panel 'Vue': ref(0) with dependency lines running to a template node and a computed node; only those light up on change.

data.label: On state change
data.b: Notify effects that read the value

lines.text: React renders with a state snapshot.
Vue tracks reactive reads and updates the effects that depend on them.

scenes.title: Refs
scenes.goal: `.value` in script, automatic unwrapping in templates.
scenes.visual: Two code cards: script card with `const count = ref(0)` and `count.value++` highlighted; template card with `{{ count }}` ticking 0 → 1 → 2.

lines.text: A ref holds a mutable value.
In script, access dot value; top-level refs unwrap in templates.

scenes.title: Computed and watch
scenes.goal: computed for pure derivation, watch for side effects with cleanup.
scenes.visual: Left card 'computed': query + tasks → filtered list. Right card 'watch': userId change fires fetch; the previous request is crossed out by onCleanup → abort().

lines.text: Use computed for pure derived state.
Use watch for side effects, and clean up stale requests.

scenes.title: Component contracts
scenes.goal: Props down, events up, slots for composition; composables and Pinia beside them.
scenes.visual: Parent box above child box: 'props' arrow down, 'emit' arrow up, a dashed slot frame inside the child filled by parent content. Side badges: 'useX() composable' and 'Pinia store'.

lines.text: Props, events, and slots define component contracts.
Composables share behavior; Pinia can manage shared client state.

scenes.title: Named slots
scenes.goal: children / element props in React = default and named slots in Vue.
scenes.visual: Left 'React': <Panel heading={<h2/>} actions={<Button/>}>children</Panel>. Right 'Vue': PanelCard with #heading, default and #actions regions filling in from the parent.

lines.text: Named slots are like children and element props in React.
The parent chooses content; the child owns layout.

scenes.title: Scoped slots
scenes.visual: Left 'React': renderItem={(item) => <TaskCard task={item} />}. Right 'Vue': ItemList iterates rows and passes { item } up through <template #item="{ item }">; TaskCard appears in each row.

data.label: Child owns iteration, parent owns rendering

lines.text: Scoped slots resemble render props.
The list handles iteration while its consumer chooses how each item appears.

scenes.title: Composables
scenes.goal: Composables = custom hooks; each call has its own state.
scenes.visual: A useTaskFilter(source) box returns { query, onlyOpen, visibleTasks } into two consumers, 'List view' and 'Board view', each showing a different query value.

lines.text: Composables reuse reactive behavior without markup.
Separate calls create independent state when that state lives inside the function.

scenes.title: Provide and inject
scenes.goal: Compound components via provide/inject, with explicit ownership.
scenes.visual: SelectionGroup at the top provides { selected: readonly, select() }; a tree line passes through a layout wrapper to two SelectionOption buttons; 'Board' toggles to pressed.

lines.text: Compound components can use provide and inject.
Keep state ownership explicit and expose actions for updates.

scenes.title: Compose in a higher layer
scenes.goal: Entities stay independent of features; a higher layer composes them.
scenes.visual: TaskWorkspace (widget) slots CompleteTaskButton (feature) into TaskCard's #actions slot (entity). A struck-through arrow from TaskCard to the feature.

lines.text: Compose entity display and feature actions in a higher layer.
The task card should not depend on the completion feature.

scenes.title: Feature-Sliced Design
scenes.goal: FSD layers apply unchanged to Vue; public APIs per slice.
scenes.visual: Layer stack app, pages, widgets, features, entities, shared; example paths slide in: pages/tasks, features/complete-task, entities/task, shared/ui; each slice shows an index.ts gate.

lines.text: Feature-Sliced Design applies to Vue too.
Organize by responsibility and expose public APIs rather than importing internal files.

scenes.title: Import rules
scenes.goal: Dependencies only point down; siblings are coordinated above.
scenes.visual: features/complete-task → entities/task arrow turns green; features/complete-task → features/delete-task arrow turns red; pages/tasks above connects to both features.

lines.text: Across slices, dependencies point to lower layers.
A page or widget coordinates sibling features.

scenes.title: Start small
scenes.visual: Project tree starts with app, pages, shared; entities and features grow in one at a time as a 'reused' tag appears.

lines.text: Start small.
Extract features when behavior is reused, and keep one-page behavior local until a useful boundary emerges.

scenes.title: Study plan
scenes.goal: A concrete next step and the companion blog.
scenes.visual: Checklist ticks one by one: reactivity, component contracts, router, testing, profiling. Ends on the blog title card 'Vue 3 for Senior React Developers'.

lines.text: Build a small task app, then add routing, tests, and performance profiling.
The accompanying blog explains each step.
